extracted.subtask_description: Assembling timely frontline dispatches, communiqués and eyewitness accounts about military operations (locations, unit actions, casualties, equipment losses, and strategic assessments) for a general newspaper audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source attribution and labeling
rubrics_metrics.description: Clearly attribute information to its source (e.g., 'A special communique Thursday General MacArthur said', 'front-line dispatches said', 'headquarters spokesman said', 'By the Associated Press').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use explicit source labels (communiqué, dispatch, spokesman, correspondent, enemy radio). Include the issuing authority, time/date and location when available. Mark unverifiable claims with verbs like 'said', 'reported' or 'claimed' rather than presenting them as established fact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness and bulletin/lead signals
rubrics_metrics.description: Mark urgent or late-developing information with clear signals such as 'BULLETIN', 'late report', 'special communique', datelines and precise timestamps (e.g., 'issued at 12230... Japanese daylight').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use bulletin labels and datelines to convey evolving situations; place the most recent/urgent updates near the top. Provide timestamps so readers can judge currency of the report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation of opposing or unconfirmed claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Report enemy or third-party claims (e.g., Red China radio broadcasts asserting strikes) while noting lack of allied confirmation when appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include both the claim and whether it is confirmed. Example: the page reports a North Korean/Chinese broadcast but explicitly says 'There was no allied confirmation of such attacks.' Avoid endorsing enemy statements without independent verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specificity of locations and unit identification
rubrics_metrics.description: Give precise place names, distances, terrain features and unit names (e.g., Taejon, Yongdok 25 miles north of Pohang, 24th Infantry Division, Maj. Gen. William F. Dean).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide geographic context (miles, relative positions, rail/highway junctions) and unit identifiers so readers can follow operational developments and strategic significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantification of losses and claims with caveats
rubrics_metrics.description: Report numbers of destroyed planes, tanks, trucks, locomotives, casualties, etc., while indicating uncertainty or possible duplication (e.g., 'destroying 15 trucks and three gun emplacements', 'Allied plane losses were put at 37', 'the toll may be higher', 'there may be some duplications').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always present numerical claims alongside qualifiers about reliability, possible duplication, and source. If figures are official claims, attribute them and note when totals are estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of eyewitness/correspondent narrative for human-interest detail
rubrics_metrics.description: Incorporate on-the-ground correspondent observations and personal quotes (e.g., veteran correspondent Whitehead's observations; pilots' first-person reports describing burning cities and attack details).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use human-interest detail to convey immediacy and the experience of combat, but continue to attribute and separate observation from confirmed facts. Place such color reporting alongside authoritative dispatches for balance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical description of weapons and equipment
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide technical and performance details when reporting new or notable weapons (e.g., the 3.5-inch rocket launcher described as larger than WWII bazooka, electrically operated, ammunition 23 inches long, no recoil; reported effectiveness against tanks).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a weapon is highlighted, include specifications, operational context (first battlefield use, reported 'knockout' results), and note whether performance claims come from official communiqués or battlefield reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategic and command-level assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Include analysis and statements from commanders about broader strategic implications (e.g., MacArthur's claim that North Koreans 'lost their chance for victory' by failing to follow up the breakthrough; advice to 'hold the Han at all costs' to buy time).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report commanders' strategic assessments verbatim and attribute them; where possible, provide context or follow-up that allows readers to judge those assessments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear description of types and effects of military actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Differentiate air strikes, naval bombardments, artillery fire, infantry-tank attacks, amphibious landings, strafing, and rocket attacks and describe their observed effects (fires, destroyed locomotives, villages shelled).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe the mode of attack and observable consequences. Use concrete examples from the field (e.g., carrier planes set fire to an oil dump; naval bombardment started big fires in Yongdok) to illustrate operational impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terrain and logistical context
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain terrain, transport nodes and supply lines' relevance (rail junctions, coastal railway/highway, valleys, mountain roads, paddy fields) and how they affect operations (e.g., attempts to cut lines to Pusan).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Connect geographic/terrain details to tactical objectives and vulnerabilities; specify why a town or route matters (rail/hwy junctions, access to beachheads, ability to cut communications).

rubrics_metrics.name: Explicit acknowledgment of uncertainty or missing information
rubrics_metrics.description: State unknowns plainly (e.g., 'the whereabouts of its commander... was unknown', 'there was no indication how many tanks the invaders...').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flag unknowns and gaps in reporting rather than filling them with speculation. Use phrases like 'unknown', 'no indication', 'appeared', 'reported' to make uncertainty explicit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrections and editorial clarifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Publish corrections or clarifications when earlier wording or figures are in error (e.g., the page includes a correction block clarifying an earlier graf).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When errors or ambiguous phrasing are discovered, issue a labeled correction that specifies the mistaken material and the corrected text. Keep corrections visible and tied to the original reporting.
